To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) three-dimensional data can be used for ASL recognition; (2) HMMs trained with three-dimensional data can yield high recognition results; (3) the use of context-dependent HMM models improves recognition results; (4) modeling transient movements between ASL signs yields better recognition results than modeling context-dependent signs; and (5) ASL recognition can benefit from using both context-dependent and transient movement models.

1) the use of context-dependent HMM models for ASL sign recognition yields better results than the use of context-free models; 2) the use of HMM models for the transient movements between signs yields better results than using HMM models for each sign individually, and 3) our recognition results, which are based on the use of three-dimensional data and the two aforementioned approaches for modeling coarticulation effects, are promising.

the use of a three-dimensional computer vision approach to ASL recognition yields better recognition results than the use of a two-dimensional approach and that the use of HMMs for continuous ASL recognition yields recognition results of 90% for a 53-sign ASL vocabulary.
